findings.finding: The 19 recorded source-gate API outcomes do not include a wrong-goal mutation, so the raw harness count remains exactly 19 and this control must not be attributed to those outcomes. The concern that semantic guard coverage was absent is resolved: frozen native/inspect regression coverage passed, and REHASHED-GOAL-REPLAY.json independently mutates the actual qualified plan, recomputes both goal digest and artifact ID, then invokes the ordinary native batch validator, which rejects it by exact source-bound input recomputation. This supplemental validation occurred at 623.518 seconds within the same 1800-second deadline, after the final memory-stop case, with no checker, Lean, source worker, retry, or cap change. This establishes semantic rejection coverage while retaining a clear harness-ordering limitation.

limitations: No claim of source fidelity beyond attributed-unreviewed authored quotes, PDE correctness, all-five-family implementation, whole-method authority, detection benefit, or task completion.
No source, Lean, tests, proof worker, or resource-limit operations were run after the intentional final memory stop; audit activity was read-only artifact inspection/hash verification.

Wrong-goal rejection was not an API outcome inside the 19-case source qualification harness; it was exercised separately by frozen native/inspect coverage and the supplemental pure native replay after the memory stop, within the original deadline. This is a harness-ordering/reporting limitation, not missing semantic guard evidence.
